passage:
A smart traffic light used cameras and sensors to adjust waiting time. If many pedestrians were waiting, it gave them more crossing time.
At first, drivers complained about longer red lights. But traffic studies showed fewer dangerous crossings and smoother flow near the school.
Students interviewed pedestrians. Older residents said they felt safer crossing the road.
The project showed that efficiency must include people outside cars.
A traffic light is a small machine with a large moral question: whose time matters? Smart systems should not only move vehicles quickly. They should protect human movement.
